subject: Regional cost sensitivity & commitment plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Morgan <alicia.morgan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Regional cost sensitivity & commitment plan

Hi Alicia — great conversation earlier. Quick written recap and a couple of concrete asks so we can put numbers against your target $/1M token band.

Recap from my side:
- Finlytics expected steady-state monthly usage: ~2M–6M total tokens (mix of gen + embeddings).
- EU data residency requirement for EU customers (roughly 30% of traffic routed to EU).
- Target unit economics you called out: roughly $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens as an acceptable range to justify product economics.

Questions / asks we need to finalize pricing options:
1) Can you confirm a nearer-term commitment horizon you prefer (POC -> short reserve -> full commit)? Example: 3-month pilot then 12-month committed baseline.
2) Can you give a rough split of inference text-generation vs embeddings (percent)? This materially changes cost cadence.
3) Average prompt + generation length estimate (tokens per request) and typical embedding dimension / frequency if available.

Notes on regional premium (initial guidance):
- US baseline pricing will be our lowest unit cost; EU region typically carries a premium driven by instance sizing, inter-region egress, and operator overhead. Ballpark uplift we expect to see is in the ~20–30% range depending on whether you require Private deployment (VPC/KMS) or can accept hosted EU region with standard residency controls.

Next steps I propose:
- If you can answer the three bullets above, we’ll produce a two-option pricing proposal: On-demand vs Reserved (3mo and 12mo tiers) showing blended $/1M tokens per region and expected monthly spend.
- I’ll attach our pricing workbook so you can poke numbers.

Attached: redwood-pricing-breakdown-v2.xlsx (workbook with tiered math).

If this looks good, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up on Fri to walk the workbook with your procurement lead.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Morgan <alicia.morgan@finlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Finlytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:43:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Regional cost sensitivity & commitment plan

Jonas — thanks for the recap, very helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- Commitment horizon: we want to run a 6-week technical POC (non-committed) and then be ready to move into a committed model if performance and residency checks out. Our procurement team prefers 12-months for price stability but if you have a 6-mo intermediate option that might work.
- Volume: estimate 2M tokens/mo in Q1 ramping to ~5–6M/mo within 6–9 months if results are good.
- Workload split: ~75% text-gen (customer-facing completions), ~25% embeddings (search & rerank).
- Average sequence length: prompts + replies average ~450 tokens per request; generation breadown varies but avg generation ~220 tokens.

On residency: about 30% of traffic must be served from EU hosts due to our EEA customers. We will require EU-hosted inference and audit logs for those flows; HSM/KMS is not mandatory but is preferred.

Procurement note (copied): we’ll need a sample SOW and a summary of SLA terms (availability/latency targets) to start legal review. Also: can you provide the expected $/1M token ranges for US-hosted and EU-hosted for the committed tiers you mentioned? That will help us budget.

Attaching a short internal one-pager that outlines their budget guardrails and the procurement checklist for vendors.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Morgan
Head of Product | Finlytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Morgan <alicia.morgan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Regional cost sensitivity & commitment plan

Alicia — perfect, thanks for the detailed numbers. A couple quick clarifying questions so our pricing work is accurate: 

- The 75/25 split: is that by token count or by request count? (Would assume token count but want to confirm.)
- Is the 30% EU residency a stable steady-state assumption or front-loaded during EU customer onboarding?
- For the POC, do you expect the EU traffic to be included (i.e., require EU-hosted responses during POC) or can POC be US-hosted with migration planned for production?

If POC can run US-hosted, it lets us show better unit economics during evaluation and gives you a short runway to validate features before incurring the EU premium. If EU-hosted is required from day one, we’ll reflect the premium in the POC run rate and include a migration checklist.

I’ll loop in Marissa on the formal pricing options; she’ll draft three candidate tiers (on-demand, 3-mo reserve, 12-mo reserve) with blended $/1M tokens for US and EU. Expect a short note back by EOD tomorrow with numbers and a suggested proposal structure to hand to procurement.

On the SOW/SLA: we can provide a standard SOW draft and our SLA summary; will attach with the pricing deliverable.

Best,
Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Regional cost sensitivity & commitment plan

Jonas — drafting the pricing options below; this is internal guidance you can share as a starting point with Alicia. I kept it conservative on uplift for EU until we know whether Private deployment is required.

Baseline assumptions (apply to blended workload you shared):
- Baseline US hosted: $1,000 per 1M tokens (this is our mid-tier committed baseline at modest volume).
- EU hosted premium: +22% for hosted EU region with standard residency controls (audit logs, region scoping). If Private (VPC + customer-managed KMS) required, uplift becomes +28–32% (includes infra & security ops).

Suggested tiers to present:
1) On-demand (no commit): US = $1,350 / 1M; EU = $1,650 / 1M (higher because no volume guarantee).
2) 3-month reserved (minimum 3mo commit): US = $995 / 1M; EU = $1,210 / 1M.
3) 12-month reserved (recommended for price stability): US = $550 / 1M; EU = $670 / 1M.

Notes:
- Discounts scale with minimum monthly committed tokens; the 12-month tier assumes a minimum blended commit that approximates 3–4M tokens/mo.
- Embeddings have lower per-token compute density but frequent small calls — we model embeddings separately in the workbook; blended numbers above assume the 75/25 split by token count.
- Data-transfer/egress between regions may add nominal fees if routing patterns are complex; call this out in the SOW.

Action items for Jonas:
- Share these three tiers with Alicia along with the attached workbook and an example SOW/SLA.
- Propose the 30–45 minute pricing walkthrough with procurement next Tue or Wed.

I attached an updated pricing workbook and a short SOW template: finlytics-commitment-checklist.pdf, redwood-pricing-breakdown-v2.xlsx.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
